videos.title: How an Ellipse Gathers Reflected Paths #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: A ray reaches the second focus after reflection; the first changed direction demonstrates the question.
editorial.mechanism: The fixed focal sum is unfolded; the perpendicular bisector and strict triangle inequality identify the tangent. Equal-angle cues explain the focal reflection under geometric idealization.
editorial.readability: Comparison paths, tangent, focal points and captions remain separate in inspected previews. Supporting construction strokes are faint and require attention.
editorial.pacing: About 98 seconds with four authored 1.1-second paragraph pauses; the proof remains the most demanding passage.
editorial.sound: Dry local narration. Full decode and independent ASR differences reviewed. No subjective listening or claim of pleasing prosody.
editorial.remaining_weaknesses: The helper-line proof is harder than the opening observation. A novice may need a closer view of the reflected endpoints and a clearer visual indication of which path is being compared. No actual learner or retention evidence.
editorial.audience_evidence: Not measured. No retention, recognition, learning or subscription results yet.

videos.title: A Circle and a Spring Share One Rhythm #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: A point and its projected shadow immediately move together, showing the relationship before naming it.
editorial.mechanism: Unequal projected steps lead to harmonic motion; restoring acceleration follows displacement. The amplitude comparison uses equal angular speed for its two demonstration turns.
editorial.readability: Circle, shadow, spring and projected arrows stay distinct; zero force removes the arrow without corrupting its renderer object.
editorial.pacing: About 90 seconds with authored paragraph pauses. Demonstrations stop at selected states and use illustrative angular speeds in different shots; this is not an uninterrupted physical simulation.
editorial.sound: Dry local narration. Full decode and independent ASR differences reviewed. No subjective listening or claim of pleasing prosody.
editorial.remaining_weaknesses: The force explanation has several successive representations. Freezing the center state can interrupt the felt rhythm, even when it helps inspect zero force. A continuous shared phase clock could better preserve the physical intuition.
editorial.audience_evidence: Not measured. No retention, recognition, learning or subscription results yet.

videos.title: The Quiet Journey Inside a Ring #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: The ring visibly grows from a circular sweep, replacing a less explanatory fade-in.
editorial.mechanism: Cross-sectional area times centroid journey is justified by paired equal-area pieces with average radius R. The rotation axis stays outside the disk.
editorial.readability: The axis and radii, paired pieces, formulas and captions remain separate. A premature full surface before the final sweep was repaired.
editorial.pacing: About 95 seconds; paired pieces and average journey receive separate holds, and the final sweep completes within speech duration.
editorial.sound: Dry local narration. Full decode and independent ASR differences reviewed. No subjective listening or claim of pleasing prosody.
editorial.remaining_weaknesses: The little pieces and the three-dimensional ring are presented in different views. The viewer must mentally link them. The proof would be more tangible if two colored swept tubes stayed attached to their source pieces.

videos.title: When Straight Lines Become Circular Arcs #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: The opening promises a line-to-circle change but spends its first section explaining reciprocal point pairs.
editorial.mechanism: Reciprocal radii, similar right triangles and a fixed diameter explain the circular image. The center exclusion and lines through the center are explicitly distinguished.
editorial.readability: Moved labels away from the construction and removed the 2-to-one-half example when the points reached the unit circle. The final grid gives the rule an expressive result.
editorial.pacing: About 91 seconds with paragraph pauses. The circle result appears around the middle after defining the mapping.
editorial.sound: Dry local narration. Full decode and independent ASR differences reviewed. No subjective listening or claim of pleasing prosody.
editorial.remaining_weaknesses: The result arrives too late for the most casual viewer. A faithful first-seconds preview of the transformed line would make the promise concrete. Similar-triangle reasoning still assumes some geometric familiarity.
editorial.audience_evidence: Not measured. No retention, recognition, learning or subscription results yet.

videos.title: A Crescent Is a Relationship with Light #math #Shorts

editorial.opening: A crescent in a restrained dark panel gives an immediate recognizable phenomenon.
editorial.mechanism: The visible disk tracks the overlap of the Earth-facing and sunlit hemispheres. Quarter and full phases, a projected terminator, and explicit eclipse/tilt caveats support the model.
editorial.readability: The upper phase view and lower orbit remain separated from captions. Warm paper surrounds a dark viewing field without decorative clutter.
editorial.pacing: About 99 seconds with paragraph pauses. Phase changes settle before the next explanation; the closing cycle is deliberately accelerated.
editorial.sound: Dry local narration. Full decode and independent ASR differences reviewed. No subjective listening or claim of pleasing prosody.
editorial.remaining_weaknesses: The two views still require mental rotation. The Moon is an ideal illuminated-area drawing rather than a textured brightness rendering; hemisphere and observer orientation conventions could be made more explicit. The panel is elegant, but that is an editorial judgment, not a measured viewer response.
editorial.audience_evidence: Not measured. No retention, recognition, learning or subscription results yet.
